Is there a brew method that you find superior? Why?
What's your opinion on the Aeropress?
I've got one and love it. The coffee it makes is the benchmark I use to compare other brews I try. I usually do the "upside-down" method with very finely ground coffee and a very short steep time.

I'm not too keen on putting really hot liquids into plastics.

I'd be all over it if they made a glass version though! Until then I'll stick to my chemex and french press.

Chemical leaching accelerates with heat, and we're finding that even polypropylene (which the aeropress is made almost entirely of) which is BPA-free will still leach other stuff that's no good for you.

I just think it makes sense to minimize contact where possible.

It's a great little device. Easy to use, super easy to clean, and makes a great cup of coffee. There's also a ton of different things you can experiment with on it to fine tune it to your bean. The only downside is that it only makes one small cup of coffee at a time. Great for one person, pain in the ass if you want more than one cup. If I want more I just use my french press.

Love the Aeropress, but I think it a little bit limiting in volume. Generally, when I use it, I use 20g of coffee to 230g of water, which about fills it up. Then I top it off with about another 20-50g of water depending on how I'm feeling and how strong I want it.

However, when I make coffee in the morning with an pour over method such as the Chemex of V60, I prefer to use a ratio of 28g of coffee to 420g of water. This yields the amount of coffee that I prefer in the mornings.

That's all. Other than that, it makes an amazing cup of coffee and usually does an amazing job of extracting flavors from certain beans that you don't get with other brew methods.

I love my Aeropress. I keep it at work and it even makes generic whole bean coffees taste great. I've used it with Nabob whole beans as well as Kicking Horse and both came out better than either French press or drip. The only other method that comes close to the flavour I get with Aeropress is if I use percolator.
I worked at a cafe that served Aeropress. Slow for a busy cafe, but a pretty easy quick way to get a great cup of coffee. Much more for home use than cafe use.
I can see how it would slow things down a bit at a cafe. Do you think it slows things down any more than one of those Japanese vacuum things or a pour-over?

No, it's definitely not slower than the japanese vacuum things. Cleaning the Aeropresses in between uses was one of the real bottlenecks. We had 8 of them, but during the rush hours, we had to devote 1 person to simply cleaning aeropresses. But pour over I would think could be quicker than the Aeropress..
Never really thought of the cleaning angle, good point.
I like it, though it takes me a while to find my sweet spot to make good coffee with it every single day if I'm not making it every day the same way.
